$comment: Cortex MCP discovery document, generated by scripts/gen_agent_index.py. Our own format: no standard yet defines a tool list at /.well-known/mcp.json. The standard pre-connection metadata is the SEP-2127 MCP Server Card at serverCard (linked from /.well-known/ai-catalog.json); tools here mirror GET /api/tools.
name: cortex
title: Cortex
description: Cortex is an open-source (MIT) MCP server and studio for training robot policies with an AI agent, built on LeRobot, MuJoCo, ACT (Action Chunking Transformer) and the SO-101 (SO-ARM101) arm. Your coding agent describes the robot arm and the task over the Model Context Protocol; Cortex builds a MuJoCo simulation, collects simulator-verified demonstrations, trains an ACT or SmolVLA policy and evaluates it, with a human approving every step that costs money or moves hardware.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project for the built-in cube task only (for any other object use start_intake); returns task spec, success criteria and an initial demonstration plan.

task_prompt.description: What the robot should learn, in plain language

tools.name: get_project_state
tools.description: Counts, datasets, training jobs, evaluations, open recommendations and next actions.

tools.name: list_episodes
tools.description: List recorded demonstrations with condition, seed, success and quality flags.

tools.name: record_demonstrations
tools.description: Record scripted-expert demonstrations in MuJoCo for the given conditions (simulation only; cube_region applies to the built-in cube task only).

auto_accept.description: accept demos that succeed and pass quality checks

wait_s.description: block up to this many seconds for completion

tools.name: analyze_dataset
tools.description: Run quality checks, telemetry failure analysis and VLM hypotheses; builds failure clusters.

tools.name: get_failure_clusters
tools.description: Current failure clusters with source (quality/evaluation/vlm), episodes and uncertainty.

tools.name: recommend_demonstrations
tools.description: Rank which demonstrations to collect next (and augment/train/evaluate suggestions) with evidence and support level.

tools.name: create_dataset_version
tools.description: Snapshot accepted episodes as a versioned LeRobotDataset v3 with lineage, train/eval split and optional image-only augmentation.

augmentation_preset.description: brightness x2, color temperature and shadow views of each train episode

tools.name: propose_training_job
tools.description: Propose an ACT/SmolVLA training job with config and resource estimate (does not start it).

tools.name: launch_training_job
tools.description: Launch an approved training job. Refused unless a human approved it in the studio or a valid operator approval_token is given.

approval_token.description: operator token; otherwise approve in the studio

tools.name: launch_simulation_evaluation
tools.description: Evaluate a policy in parallel MuJoCo branches: baseline, shifted object, dim lighting. Records seeds, successes, rewards and videos.

tools.name: compare_experiments
tools.description: Branch-by-branch comparison of evaluation runs with deltas and p-values.

tools.name: get_next_actions
tools.description: What to do next for this project, and why.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Status/progress of a background job.

tools.name: create_policy_project
tools.description: Create a project for a manipulation policy and (by default) start autonomous agent demonstration collection (our self-hosted VLM, or GPT-6 Astra) within the planner budget.

task_prompt.description: e.g. 'Train an SO-101 policy to pick up a cube and place it in a bowl'

model_budget_usd.description: planner spend cap; can only lower the server default, never raise it

tools.name: start_agent_collection
tools.description: Generate demonstrations autonomously: the agent planner (self-hosted VLM or GPT-6 Astra) plans from camera images, validated IK executes in MuJoCo, simulator-verified successes become LeRobot episodes. Returns job_id.

conditions.description: target these cells only (e.g. a weak condition)

tools.name: get_collection_progress
tools.description: Status, successes, failures, model calls and spend of a collection.

tools.name: get_demonstration_results
tools.description: Per-attempt outcomes with provenance (agent planner model vs scripted oracle), usage and recoveries, plus per-collector metrics.

tools.name: train_from_agent_demonstrations
tools.description: Build a dataset version from agent-generated demos and propose ACT training (training itself needs approval). Returns job_id.

tools.name: evaluate_learned_policy
tools.description: Evaluate a trained checkpoint (never the oracle) in the three parallel MuJoCo conditions.

checkpoint_id.description: a trained checkpoint (not the scripted oracle)

tools.name: import_demonstrations
tools.description: Import existing human/robot demonstrations from a LeRobot dataset on the Hugging Face Hub (the user's own SO-101 recordings or public ones). Returns job_id.

repo_id.description: Hugging Face dataset repo id, e.g. 'lerobot/svla_so101_pickplace' or the user's own 'user/my_so101_demos'

tools.name: get_infrastructure
tools.description: Where this project's stages run: planner, training backend (Futurama GPU or manual), GPU and walltime, evaluation and robot, each with live availability and the reason when unavailable.

tools.name: set_infrastructure
tools.description: Change this project's infrastructure choices (planner, training backend, GPU, walltime). Only stores the choice: training still needs the human's approval.

tools.name: robot_start_episode
tools.description: Simulated arm (MuJoCo, no hardware): start an SO-101 episode you will control yourself (fresh seed; optional cube region/lighting). Returns session_id.

tools.name: robot_act
tools.description: Simulated arm (MuJoCo, no hardware): run one validated robot tool in your session (observe_scene, get_robot_state, propose_grasp, move_end_effector, set_gripper, verify_grasp, place_object, check_task_success).

tools.name: robot_finish_episode
tools.description: Simulated arm (MuJoCo, no hardware): end your episode; the simulator judges success and successes become demonstrations.

tools.name: improve_policy
tools.description: Find the weakest measured condition, collect targeted agent demos there in fresh seeds, build a new dataset version and propose retraining. Returns job_id.

tools.name: start_intake
tools.description: Start describing a robot-learning task: creates a draft project and returns typed questions (each with a ready-to-send patch) about the arm, cameras, objects, place zones, environment and task.

prompt.description: The task in plain language, e.g. 'pick up the water bottle and put it on the coaster'. Objects named here are pre-filled from a catalogue.

mode.description: 'sim' (the MVP runs everything in physics sim) or 'real'

tools.name: update_intake
tools.description: Answer intake questions by merging a partial spec. Returns the merged spec, what changed, what is still assumed, and the remaining questions.

patch.description: Partial intake spec to merge. Each open question carries a ready-to-send patch; lists of objects/zones/cameras/obstacles merge by name. Sizes in metres: box = [x, y, z] full extents, cylinder = [diameter, height] (not radius), sphere = [diameter]. Positions: +x away from the arm base, +y to its left, z up from the table.

tools.name: get_intake_status
tools.description: The intake spec, open questions, and whether the sim scene is built.

tools.name: build_simulation
tools.description: Build the MuJoCo scene from the completed intake, then check feasibility (jaw opening, payload torque, reach to every start and zone, with alternatives). Returns a top-camera preview.

tools.name: capture_frame
tools.description: Render a scene camera (valid: top, front, wrist_cam) so you can check the sim matches the real setup you described.

tools.name: get_policy_weaknesses
tools.description: Where the trained policy is weak, measured from its latest sim evaluation: per condition the success rate with a Wilson 95% interval and n, failure modes from sim telemetry, start-state clusters, and VLM hypotheses (unverified). Ranked by the gap that holds at the upper bound.

checkpoint_id.description: a trained checkpoint; default: the latest evaluated one

target.description: success rate a condition should reach

tools.name: propose_rl_sandboxes
tools.description: Propose one RL sandbox per top weakness (skill-parameter RL with CEM, which tunes the validated IK skill; its successful rollouts become targeted demos for retraining ACT). Each runs a measured pilot as a job, then reports the pilot, predicted sandbox success, predicted policy uplift, P(uplift >= delta), regression elsewhere, cost (episodes, CPU hours, $) and assumptions. Predictions are labelled estimates with their source (measured, prior or learned).

budget.description: SandboxBudget overrides: iterations (<=15), population, pilot_episodes, demos, heldout_episodes, max_parallel

wait_s.description: wait up to this long for the pilots to finish

tools.name: accept_rl_sandboxes
tools.description: Start sandboxes whose pilot has finished. Local CPU sandboxes cost $0 and you may accept them within budget_cap and the project's standing budget. GPU or paid sandboxes return approval_required: a human approves them in the studio.

budget_cap.description: the most you allow these sandboxes to cost, in USD. Local CPU sandboxes cost $0

max_cpu_hours.description: optional cap on estimated CPU hours

tools.name: get_rl_sandbox_status
tools.description: Live progress of one sandbox or all of a project's: phase, CEM iteration, episodes, success with interval, elite parameters, the current randomization ranges, elapsed time, cost so far; when finished, the measured held-out result (base vs tuned on matched seeds, McNemar p) and demos.

tools.name: stop_rl_sandbox
tools.description: Stop a sandbox. A running one stops after its current CEM iteration, still evaluates what it has on held-out seeds, and reports why it stopped.

tools.name: collection_snapshot
tools.description: Live snapshot of an agent demonstration collection for the MCP App view: status, successes/attempts, model calls and spend, recent attempts and the latest sim frame.

collection_id.description: defaults to the project's latest collection

tools.name: evaluation_report
tools.description: Evaluation of a policy per condition, with Wilson 95% intervals, measured failure modes and the weakest condition.

evaluation_id.description: defaults to the project's latest evaluation

tools.name: review_training_job
tools.description: Show a proposed training job (cost, GPU hours, dataset, rationale) for a human to review and approve. Does not approve anything.

training_job_id.description: defaults to the latest proposed training job

tools.name: approve_training_from_view
tools.description: Human-only: approve a training job with the single-use nonce from the review view. Agents never have the nonce.

nonce.description: single-use approval nonce given only to the review view

tools.name: get_diagnosis_inputs
tools.description: Bring your own model: run quality checks and measured failure analysis, then return the keyframe contact sheets, measured telemetry and fixed-taxonomy prompt for the episodes a VLM should review. Answer them with your model and call submit_failure_hypotheses with the analysis_id.

max_targets.description: episodes to review (failed evaluation rollouts first)

tools.name: submit_failure_hypotheses
tools.description: Store your model's failure hypotheses for an analysis from get_diagnosis_inputs. Validated against the fixed taxonomy (any invalid answer rejects the submission); stored as unverified VLM hypotheses with the route and the model you report, then failure clusters are rebuilt.

category.description: one of the fixed failure taxonomy categories

confidence.description: the model's own confidence, 0-1 (not a probability)

reply_text.description: the model's raw reply; parsed and validated by Cortex

error.description: the client could not get an answer (declined, failed); recorded, never replaced by a guess

route.description: 'mcp_sampling' when the answers came from a sampling/createMessage request, 'mcp_agent' when you (the agent) looked at the contact sheets yourself

model.description: the model that produced the answers, as reported by the MCP client (sampling result `model`)

tools.name: get_session_link
tools.description: The Cortex studio URL where your human can watch this agent session live (every tool call, its arguments, results, images and approvals). Share it when you start working.
